summary: BALAM is a health monitor that adapts to the user, creating a tailored profile and taking physical factors into account for more precise monitoring. BALAM is designed for use during missions, so it can be operated almost entirely by voice, with a hands-free mode. Data never leaves the browser, since everything is stored in the cache, ensuring the security of this information throughout the mission. If the program detects something concerning, it contacts Earth to immediately send distress signals to the personnel on the ground. However, its daily analysis serves to keep track of the astronaut's health and to help prevent situations like this. It stores information through images, voice, and keyboard input, forming a fairly complete telemetry ecosystem. It includes a visual log designed to detect physical changes, which also serves as a record for each astronaut once the mission ends. Voice control is ideal for situations where a screen can't be viewed, since it not only controls the system but also communicates with the astronaut, making it fully usable without a monitor. BALAM is a complete assistant designed to work hand in hand with astronauts. It does not replace an onboard physician, but it becomes an extra layer of protection for the astronauts' well-being.
details:
BALAM is an adaptive health monitor for astronauts that builds a personalized profile and accounts for physical factors to monitor more precisely. Built for mission use, it works almost entirely by voice in a hands-free mode, and it also speaks to the astronaut, so it can be used without a screen. It collects data through images, voice, and keyboard input, forming a complete telemetry ecosystem. A visual log detects physical changes over time and serves as a record of each astronaut after the mission. All data stays in the browser's cache for security. Daily analysis helps track health and prevent problems, and if something concerning is detected, BALAM immediately contacts Earth to alert ground personnel. It doesn't replace an onboard physician, but adds an extra layer of protection for astronauts.

Benefits: BALAM supports disease prevention through an interactive 2D body diagram where astronauts can log pain and symptoms. It tracks the development of illnesses and disorders across physical, mental, and emotional health, giving complete, ongoing health control.

Intended impact: To protect astronauts' health by adding a new layer of safety during missions, helping detect and prevent problems before they become serious.

Tools: Built with React and TypeScript, with code development assisted by Microsoft Copilot, and deployed on Vercel.

Creativity: BALAM is designed around voice accessibility. If an astronaut can't look at a screen or has no monitor nearby, an intuitive bilingual (English and Spanish) voice guides them through logging their health and symptoms, making the app fully usable hands-free. Combined with a 2D body map and a visual log, it turns health tracking into a natural, accessible experience.

Factors considered: We prioritized practicality and accessibility in mission conditions (hands-free, screen-free use), English and Spanish support, data privacy by keeping all data in the browser, and a holistic view of health covering physical, mental, and emotional well-being. We also designed BALAM to complement, not replace, an onboard physician.
